concept: Short horizon momentum breakout and mean reversion
summary: Source-anchored research for Short horizon momentum breakout and mean reversion. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: In Hudson and Urquhart's daily data the edge sits on the long side. The average return from a buy signal is positive and significant for every coin and rule class, and over 90% of rules have positive buy returns for Litecoin, Ripple and both Bitcoin series. Sell-signal (short) returns are mostly negative, and in 15 of 20 rule-class-by-coin cells no rule earns a significant sell return. The sample is a strong uptrend, so part of this may be market drift. (low confidence)

Hudson and Urquhart's best in-sample rules lost money out of sample for Bitcoin. The in-sample winners were channel-breakout rules for both Bitcoin series and Litecoin, and moving-average rules for Ripple and Ethereum. In January to June 2018 both Bitcoin series had negative annualized return, Sharpe and Sortino ratios, while the other three coins stayed positive. The window is six months long and falls in a bear market, so it is a weak test in either direction. The authors suggest Bitcoin is more efficient because more investors watch it. (low confidence)

Kitron and Wengrowicz test the 15-minute reversal against measurement artifacts (their package includes flat-bar-excluded and one-bar-gap refits) and report that it survives, but the effect is small. The class-mean AUC gap between crypto and equities is +0.031 as designed and +0.011 (95% CI +0.008 to +0.014) under the most conservative accounting. The result also survives an exact permutation null and a frozen holdout. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-22)

Intraday momentum and reversal switch with market state. Wen et al. report that Bitcoin's intraday predictability pattern changes around large intraday price jumps, FOMC announcements, liquidity levels and the COVID-19 outbreak. A timing strategy built on their intraday predictors earns more economic value than always-long or buy-and-hold. Shen et al. find momentum strongest in high-volume, high-volatility sessions. Both studies point toward conditioning the momentum-or-reversal bet on volatility, volume, jump and liquidity state instead of running one static rule. (medium confidence)

Build the coin universe point-in-time. Zarattini et al. use a survivorship-bias-free dataset of all coins traded since 2015 and trade the 20 most liquid. Grobys et al. fix the 30 largest coins by market capitalization at the end of each prior December to avoid illiquid small coins, which Zaremba et al. link to daily reversal. These choices target survivorship bias and illiquid-coin artifacts. (medium confidence)

Near-zero autocorrelation does not rule out a reversal edge. In the Kitron and Wengrowicz data, lag-one return autocorrelation is near zero on major coins, yet a rule that bets against the sign of the previous 15-minute candle captures most of the effect. The authors write that the signal lives in signs, not magnitudes. A linear autocorrelation test alone can therefore miss it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-22)
